transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marisa Chen (Arbor Head of ML), Daniel Ortiz (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (Security), Lena Wu (Product), Jorge Alvarez (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation results, prompt tuning, regression checks and guardrails. Action items agreed for scoring refresh, data/security follow-ups, and scheduling dedicated latency benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check - can you all see my screen?
[00:05] Marisa: yep, seeing it, looks good.
[00:08] Ethan: great. this is our weekly POC sync, primarily quality evals. Priya and I will run through the latest scoring results you sent and then we'll talk tune recommendations and next steps.
[00:18] Priya: morning all. quick note, transcript might be a little rough, some names got munged in the auto-transcript, sorry in advance.
[00:25] Daniel: no worries.
[00:27] Priya: okay jumping in - Jorge shared the batch of 2k examples last week. we ran them through three config variants: hosted redwood base quantized, hosted with prefix caching, and a dedicated node profile. scoring uses a blended metric: 60% helpfulness (human scores), 20% factuality classifier, 20% hallucination penalty.
[00:45] Jorge: quick correction, i thought we said 50/30/20? my spreadsheet shows 50 helpfulness.
[00:50] Priya: hmm, yeah might be mismatch—our pipeline used 60/20/20 for this run, will note that as a variance.
[00:55] Marisa: okay that explains the small diffs we saw in the dashboard.
[00:58] [01:02] Ethan: show the slide - overall aggregated quality: hosted quantized avg score 0.78, hosted+cache 0.82, dedicated 0.85. latency median: hosted 120ms token, hosted+cache 90ms, dedicated 45ms. cost per 1k tokens: hosted lowest per-unit but higher tail cost under load.
[01:25] Daniel: dedicated looks best for latency and quality, as expected, but can you remind us of the commit sizes?
[01:30] Ethan: yes, dedicated is reserved capacity - our example commit for these tests was 4x A100-equivalent slots, monthly commit, and we also did a burst config for traffic spikes. pricing sketch i'll share after.
[01:38] Samir: on security—i noticed the logs show prompts and completions for evals. what's the retention by default? can we mask PHI?
[01:45] Priya: good question. by default eval logs are retained 30 days in the console; for POCs we can enable shorter retention or redact at ingest. we also support KMS-backed encryption for Private deployments.
[01:58] Samir: are we able to run the model in our VPC for the dedicated run? we need EPH and PHI to stay on-prem for compliance.
[02:05] Ethan: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages; for the POC we can simulate that with our private tenant or run a customer-managed deployment if you want. note that moving to fully on-prem triggers additional integration time.
[02:16] Marisa: what's the regression detection we have? i.e., if we change prompt templates and quality drops for a slice, how do you flag that?
[02:22] Priya: currently our eval harness runs per-prompt-set diffs and produces per-case delta scores and an alert if drop > 5% on critical metrics. we also have guardrail classifiers for hallucination and PII leakage that can run as a post-filter. for POC we've set them to alert only.
[02:35] Jorge: small nit - some of the proper nouns in results show as mismatched, likely NER errors in the classifier.
[02:40] Priya: yeah that's transcription/classifier noise; we can add targeted test cases for named entities to ensure the reg-check is robust.
[02:46] [03:00] Ethan: switching to the concrete failures - show example case list. (screen) here's a sample of 12 regressions flagged on the Intake prompt set, most are around hallucinated medication suggestions and some context truncation.
[03:15] Marisa: can you share those 12 cases? i want to check whether they are clinically meaningful or edge-cases.
[03:19] Priya: yes, sharing as a csv after. biggest cluster is when the prompt length exceeds 1.2k tokens and the model attempts to summarize preceding notes—KV-cache eviction patterns cause some context loss in the quantized path.
[03:32] Daniel: is that reproducible on dedicated?
[03:35] Priya: it's much less on dedicated because the model gets full sequence windows and optimized kernels—so less eviction. that's why dedicated scored higher.
[03:42] Samir: what's the tradeoff in cost if we choose dedicated purely for quality?
[03:45] Ethan: committed capacity raises base cost but reduces tail latency and decreases re-requests due to failures; our estimate is ~30% higher base monthly but 20-40% lower per-interaction cost once you factor in retries and SLA penalties. i'll send a detailed pricing sketch.
[03:58] [04:10] Marisa: another ask—can the guardrail classifier be tuned per customer taxonomy? we have clinical entity lists and banned-suggestion patterns.
[04:18] Priya: yes, we can add custom rules and a domain-specific hallucination classifier. the training data you provide improves precision; we recommend iterative tuning with ~500 labeled examples.
[04:28] Marisa: ok we'll scope that.
[04:30] Lena: question on scoring metrics — could you include a separate metric for 'actionability' for intake prompts?
[04:36] Priya: sure, actionability can be added as a per-case human label and folded into the blended score. it will just increase annotation cost.
[04:42] Jorge: how frequently do you run the reg-check? weekly? nightly?
[04:46] Priya: for POC we run weekly; for production customers we recommend daily diffs on critical prompt sets.
[04:50] [05:00] Ethan: ok let's talk about prompt tuning run we propose: stage 1 - constrained prompt refactors (shorter context, explicit system instructions), stage 2 - rerank candidates with a light-weight re-ranker, stage 3 - re-eval with guardrails on. expected turnaround 7-10 days for stage 1, 2 weeks for stage 2 including annotations.
[05:18] Marisa: timeline works but we need at least one clinical reviewer in the loop. i'll assign.
[05:22] [05:30] Samir: security follow-ups: can we get the SOC2 report, pen-test evidence, and encryption key flow? also we need SAML SSO for your console access.
[05:39] Ethan: yes, i'll send SOC2 and pen-test summaries. SAML can be enabled; and for KMS flows we have docs describing envelope encryption and HSM options for private deployments.
[05:49] Samir: for the POC data, we need Data Processing Agreement in place before we move to real PHI in tests.
[05:55] Ethan: understood, i'll loop legal and share the DPA template.
[05:58] [06:10] Daniel: back to results - can you show per-slice precision/recall for the factuality classifier?
[06:15] Priya: short answer - factuality precision 0.88 overall, recall 0.74, certain slices (drug names) precision dips to 0.79. detailed CSV will be attached.
[06:26] Daniel: okay we'll look for false positives where classifier flags benign creative phrasing.
[06:30] Priya: yep, tuning threshold is straightforward, but tuning thresholds trade off false negative hallucinations vs more false positives.
[06:38] [06:50] Marisa: one more operational question - if we change prompts in prod, do you support automated canary rollouts?
[06:55] Ethan: yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B rollout policies with automatic rollback based on regression thresholds you set. you can also route a small percent to a dedicated model variant.
[07:05] Marisa: good. that's useful.
[07:08] [07:20] Jorge: small transcription note - the ASR scrambled 'KV cache' as 'K V catch' in earlier emails, just FYI.
[07:25] Priya: haha noted.
[07:27] [07:35] Ethan: ok let's capture decisions and next steps. decision 1: run updated scoring with guardrail classifier integrated (Priya). decision 2: Arbor to finalize top 50 prompts for regression watchlist (Marisa). decision 3: Redwood to share SOC2 + DPA + KMS docs (Ethan). decision 4: schedule dedicated latency benchmark (Ethan+Daniel).
[07:55] Marisa: sounds right.
[07:57] [08:00] Lena: quick Q — can we tune the re-ranker to prefer shorter, less speculative answers?
[08:04] Priya: yes, re-ranker hyperparameters can penalize answer length and novelty; we'll propose a config.
[08:10] [08:20] Ethan: i will share the PR for the scoring notebook and a csv of flagged cases by tomorrow.
[08:25] Marisa: and I'll have the clinical reviewer assigned by end of day Thurs.
[08:30] Samir: i'll send compliance artifact list early next week.
[08:34] [08:40] Jorge: one last item—can we get a small sample of the dedicated run logs to inspect latencies under 95th pct?
[08:46] Priya: yes, we'll run a 2-hour benchmark and share the logs; Daniel, can you provision a traffic spec?
[08:51] Daniel: yep i'll draft and share by EOD tomorrow.
[08:55] [09:00] Ethan: awesome. any other Qs?
[09:02] Marisa: none from me.
[09:04] Ethan: cool thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and update the tracker.
[09:08] [09:12] End of recording.
